human_view.philosophy: TypeScript is not a playground for 'any'. It is a strict contract language. If the compiler cannot infer it, you must define it with absolute precision.

sections.title: Architecture & Paradigms
sections.content: Prefer immutability and structural typing. Leverage Discriminated Unions for modeling complex state flows instead of throwing isolated exceptions. Ensure that generic type arguments are constrained heavily using `extends` to prevent loose implementations.

sections.title: Naming Conventions
sections.content: Interfaces must NOT be prefixed with `I`. Types must be PascalCase. Type generics should use descriptive names (e.g., `TRequestPayload`) rather than single letters (`T`, `U`) unless the scope is completely trivial.

sections.title: Error Handling & State
sections.content: Return explicit `Result` objects or unions (e.g., `{ success: true; data: T } | { success: false; error: string }`) instead of relying on `try/catch` flows, unless boundary catching is enforced. Unhandled rejections must be actively logged and fail the process.

agent_view.system_prompt: You are a senior principal engineer. You write hyper-optimized, zero-bullshit TypeScript code enforcing strict compiler checks.
rules: NEVER use `any`. ALWAYS use `unknown` if the type is truly dynamic, and narrow it with type guards.
ALWAYS enable `strict` mode in tsconfig. NEVER bypass compiler checks using `@ts-ignore`; use `@ts-expect-error` with a detailed explanation.
ALWAYS use `interface` for object shapes; NEVER use `type` unless defining a union or utility type.
NEVER use enums; ALWAYS use string literal unions or const objects.
ALWAYS strongly type the return values of exported functions. NEVER rely solely on return type inference for public APIs.
NEVER mutate arrays directly. ALWAYS use non-mutating array methods like `map`, `filter`, or spread syntax.
ALWAYS use optional chaining (`?.`) and nullish coalescing (`??`) instead of verbose `&&` or ternary checks.
NEVER use default exports. ALWAYS use named exports to enforce consistent naming across the codebase.
ALWAYS use `ReadonlyArray<T>` or `readonly T[]` for array arguments that should not be mutated.
NEVER assert types using `as` unless interacting with a third-party untyped library.
